suggestions.title: Monday: the full lower sheet — calves haven't trained in four weeks, hams and abs in three

rationale.science: Two weeks off costs a trained lifter almost no strength; by three to four weeks it starts to show — reps before load — and it comes back within a session or two of resuming (Bosquet 2013; Mujika & Padilla 2000). In a deficit the lifting is what tells the body to keep the muscle: defend load, don't chase volume (Schoenfeld 2017).
rationale.data: Last outings on file: calves 8/10 (320 × 11,11,10,8) · ham curl 8/14 (125 × 11,9,9) · crunch 8/14 (100 × 14,14,14) · leg raise 8/14 (7,6) · hack 8/21 (200 × 8,7,8) · hip thrust 8/21 (90 × 7,8,7) · extension 8/21 (160 × 8,8). Friday's lower day did not run. Thursday's upper day held every load with the back halves 13% short.
rationale.relationship: Thursday showed the layoff shape — first sets match, later sets go. The legs are one to two weeks further out, so expect more of it: hack, extension and hip thrust first sets within a rep or two; calves, hams and abs two to three short. That's a baseline, not a decline. A hold only comes from a zero-reps-in-reserve opener that misses — open at two.

suggestions.predict: A lower session logged by Tuesday 9/08 with all seven lifts at the loads on file and 2-RIR openers: hack, extension and hip thrust first sets within two reps of 8/21, no hold flags; calves, ham and crunch first sets two to three reps under their last outing. If any of those three matches outright, the rust is smaller than I think and I'll say so. No lower session by 9/09: miss on the ask, and three straight lower days missed becomes a coach flag, not a card.

suggestions.title: The app's quad card (10 → 12 sets): not before Monday's lower day has run once at the current sets

rationale.science: No trial has found that more volume during a deficit buys more muscle (Roth 2023; Nait-Yahia 2026 — the card's own citations). Returns per set flatten past roughly 5–10 weekly sets (Pelland 2025), and in a cut each extra set is paid for out of recovery you don't have.
rationale.data: The card fired 9/04 on 'scale stalled, lifts not falling, recovery green, sleep clean.' Sleep: real — 8.17, 8.08, 8.25 h on 8/31–9/02. Stall: three morning reads in fifteen days. Lifts: one upper session, six of seven short on reps. Extension last trained 8/21 (160 × 8,8). The same day, the app printed 'volume band sits above the high-return region — tighten to 6–12.'
rationale.relationship: A third extension set on its first outing in seventeen days can't be read — the set, or the rust — which is the exact problem the August 10 hand-back you approved was built to avoid. Run Monday at two sets, get one clean read, then decide. Not a no — a not-yet, and a coach conversation either way.

suggestions.predict: Monday runs at the current two extension sets and the first set lands at or near 8 at 160: 'lifts not falling' is confirmed on a real read and the card can be judged next week on clean ground. If a third set goes in before that read, expect extension entries of 3 on the session and a 'did not convert' verdict within two lower days that neither of us can assign a cause. No lower session: nothing to grade, rides.

suggestions.title: Monday morning, before legs: one scale read — Friday and Saturday were blank and the 161.1 is still unanswered

rationale.science: A single morning read is noise around a slow trend — for you, ±1.46 lb day to day — which is why one read never decides anything and why the trend needs a steady supply of them. The rate of loss, the thing this whole cut steers on, can't be measured across a window that's mostly blank.
rationale.data: Reads since 8/21: 8/31 164.0 · 9/01 163.4 · 9/03 161.1 — three in fifteen days; 9/04 and 9/05 blank. Your app shows 162.9, I show 163.1, both carrying on the 161.1 with nothing since. The app's rate line prints 0.03 lb/wk — a placeholder.
rationale.relationship: Thursday's 161.1 was the lowest read in the file, two pounds under the trend, and both instruments damped it as a spike. Low 162s or under on Monday and the trend follows it down — August was fat. 163 to 164 and it was a light morning. Either answer is fine; no answer keeps the rate unpriceable and the maintenance estimate shrinking.

suggestions.predict: A read dated 9/07 or 9/08 lands. At or under 162.5: your app's trend moves under 162.9 within two reads and I call August's drop mostly fat. 163.0–164.0: the trend holds 162.9–163.3 and Thursday was a light morning. No read by 9/09: miss on the ask, and scale asks move into the brief only until a contact-day pattern returns.
